balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Poly Property Services Co., Ltd.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash, time deposits and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents and time deposits (fixed-term bank deposits, typically >3 months, booked separately from cash) against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Poly Property Services Co., Ltd.: the company carries essentially zero debt and parks a large share of its cash pile in time deposits -- counting only the "Cash & equivalents" line understates the liquid balance sheet by roughly as much again.

What to watch:

  • Combined cash + time deposits versus payables owed to related parties (Poly Developments)
  • Time deposits shifting to cash ahead of a dividend or buyback

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Poly Property Services Co., Ltd.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Poly Property Services Co., Ltd.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Poly Property Services Co., Ltd.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

gfa.title: Managed and contracted GFA
gfa.content:
Managed GFA is the gross floor area currently under management contracts generating fee revenue -- the property-services equivalent of a subscriber count. Contracted GFA adds area signed but not yet handed over for management, so it leads managed GFA and is the forward-pipeline indicator.

For Poly Property Services Co., Ltd.: this is an asset-light, fee-for-service business -- revenue growth ultimately traces back to GFA growth times fee rate, not to capital deployed. Third-party (non-Poly-Group) GFA is now the larger and faster-growing share, which matters because it is not guaranteed by the parent developer's own build-out.

What to watch:

  • Contracted GFA converting into managed GFA with a lag, not stalling
  • Growth increasingly reliant on third-party wins versus Poly Group handovers, as the broader China property downturn slows the latter
  • Managed GFA growth outrunning or lagging revenue growth (a sign of fee-rate pressure either way)

netIncomeNci.title: Net income: attributable vs including non-controlling interests
netIncomeNci.content:
Net income (attributable) is the portion of profit belonging to Poly Property's own shareholders. Net income including NCI adds the share of profit earned by subsidiaries that are consolidated but only partly owned (common where the company holds a controlling but not 100% stake in a local project company or community-services JV).

For Poly Property Services Co., Ltd.: the gap between the two lines is the minority-interest cash flow that never reaches the parent -- the DCF values the attributable line, not the consolidated one, so a widening gap here is dilution investors should price in even though it never shows up in consolidated revenue.

What to watch:

  • NCI share of profit growing faster than attributable profit (minority partners capturing more of the growth)
  • Sudden jumps from new JV consolidations or stake changes

segmentRevenue.title: Revenue mix: property services vs other
segmentRevenue.content:
Property services revenue is the recurring, fee-based core (managing residential, commercial and public properties) -- plotted against total revenue, which also includes project-based value-added services to developers (pre-delivery, office leasing, mostly to parent Poly Group) and community value-added services to residents (retail, housekeeping, brokerage).

For Poly Property Services Co., Ltd.: property services is roughly 80% of revenue and growing, while the lower-margin developer-services slice is shrinking with the real-estate downturn; community value-added services, though a small slice, carries the highest gross margin (~40-47% vs ~14-16% for core property management) and is the main margin lever.

What to watch:

  • Property services share of revenue rising (higher revenue quality, more recurring)
  • Community value-added services growing as a share, since it carries the fattest margin

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Poly Property Services Co., Ltd.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Poly Property Services Co., Ltd.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Poly Property Services Co., Ltd.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Poly Property Services Co., Ltd.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Poly Property Services Co., Ltd.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
